sources.population_or_scope: More than 158,000 recreational marathon runners with app-recorded training
sources.notes: Associates disciplined multiweek reductions with better marathon outcomes; observational design, selection, and training-history confounding prevent causal individualized rules.

sources.citation: Lipková L, Struhár I, Krajňák J, Puda D, Kumstát M. Field-based tests for determining critical speed among runners and its practical application: a systematic review. Front Sports Act Living. 2025;7:1520914.
sources.title: Field-based tests for determining critical speed among runners and its practical application: a systematic review
sources.population_or_scope: Field-based critical-speed testing protocols in runners
sources.notes: Finds multiple field protocols with high reliability under specified conditions; protocol, mathematical model, test number/order, and environment affect estimates, especially D-prime.

sources.citation: Maffulli N, Padulo J, Oliva F. Noninvasive assessment of the anaerobic threshold in endurance athletes: an evidence-based narrative review of methods, validity, and field feasibility. Br Med Bull. 2026;160(1):ldag037.
sources.title: Noninvasive assessment of the anaerobic threshold in endurance athletes: an evidence-based narrative review of methods, validity, and field feasibility
sources.population_or_scope: Eighty-eight reports comparing noninvasive threshold methods with criterion methods in endurance athletes
sources.notes: Methods may correlate at group level without individual interchangeability; threshold definitions and protocols differ, and agreement/reliability matter more than correlation alone.

sources.citation: Anderson M, Bellenger C, Sabapathy S, Arnold B, Bellinger P. The measurement and application of critical speed and D-prime in running: a scoping review. Sports Med. 2026;56(7):1637-1674.
sources.title: The measurement and application of critical speed and D-prime in running: a scoping review
sources.population_or_scope: Running critical-speed and D-prime protocols, models, performance prediction, and training prescription
sources.notes: Critical speed can support performance modelling and prescription, but protocol/model choices and variable D-prime estimates require transparent method storage and cautious individual use.

sources.citation: Hecksteden A, Pitsch W, Rosenberger F, Meyer T. Repeated testing for the assessment of individual response to exercise training. J Appl Physiol. 2018;124(6):1567-1579.
sources.title: Repeated testing for the assessment of individual response to exercise training
sources.source_type: controlled training trial and methods comparison
sources.population_or_scope: 36 healthy untrained adults; one-year walking/jogging program with repeated VO2max testing
sources.notes: Responder classifications disagreed substantially across methods, illustrating measurement/day-to-day variability and the danger of declaring individual nonresponse from one pre/post comparison.

sources.citation: Bonafiglia JT, Preobrazenski N, Gurd BJ. A systematic review examining the approaches used to estimate interindividual differences in trainability and classify individual responses to exercise training. Front Physiol. 2021;12:665044.
sources.title: A systematic review examining the approaches used to estimate interindividual differences in trainability and classify individual responses to exercise training
sources.population_or_scope: Methods used in exercise-training studies to estimate response heterogeneity and classify responders
sources.notes: Highlights inconsistent analytical approaches and misclassification risk; supports repeated/comparative evidence rather than fixed responder identities.

sources.citation: Buchheit M, Laursen PB. High-intensity interval training, solutions to the programming puzzle: Part I: cardiopulmonary emphasis. Sports Med. 2013;43(5):313-338.
sources.title: High-intensity interval training, solutions to the programming puzzle: Part I: cardiopulmonary emphasis
sources.population_or_scope: High-intensity interval programming variables and acute cardiopulmonary responses across athlete populations
sources.notes: Interval response depends on interacting work, recovery, modality, repetition, and set variables; time near VO2max is only one consideration.

sources.citation: Buchheit M, Laursen PB. High-intensity interval training, solutions to the programming puzzle: Part II: anaerobic energy, neuromuscular load and practical applications. Sports Med. 2013;43(10):927-954.
sources.title: High-intensity interval training, solutions to the programming puzzle: Part II: anaerobic energy, neuromuscular load and practical applications
sources.population_or_scope: High-intensity interval programming, anaerobic contribution, neuromuscular/musculoskeletal load, and periodization
sources.notes: Similar cardiorespiratory sessions can have different anaerobic and mechanical costs; elite example volumes are not recreational prescriptions.

sources.citation: Midgley AW, McNaughton LR. Time at or near VO2max during continuous and intermittent running: a review with special reference to considerations for the optimisation of training protocols to elicit the longest time at or near VO2max. J Sports Med Phys Fitness. 2006;46(1):1-14.
sources.title: Time at or near VO2max during continuous and intermittent running
sources.population_or_scope: Continuous and intermittent running protocols intended to elicit time at or near VO2max
sources.notes: Shows how interval design affects time near VO2max but explicitly notes that multiple adaptations and further experimental evidence should guide competitive-running recommendations.

sources.citation: Barbieri A, Fuk A, Gallo G, et al. Cardiorespiratory and metabolic consequences of detraining in endurance athletes. Front Physiol. 2024;14:1334766.
sources.title: Cardiorespiratory and metabolic consequences of detraining in endurance athletes
sources.population_or_scope: Endurance-trained athletes experiencing short- or long-term training cessation/reduction
sources.notes: Complete or substantial training cessation can reduce cardiorespiratory/metabolic adaptations within weeks; magnitude depends on prior training, duration, and retained stimulus, so no universal loss timetable follows.
